sections.heading: [ O, A, B, B, A, O ]

content:
✧ MIROGLYPH NARRATIVE ARCHITECTURE PRIMER (v3) ✧
A recursive symbolic system for nonlinear mythic storytelling and ritual design.
The Miroglyph is a narrative architecture of 18 symbolic nodes, formed by the intersection of 3 Arcs and 6 universal Conditions. Each node is a mythic state or recursion point that can manifest as a character, force, space, feeling, pattern, or compositional move across mediums.

Core structure
I. Three narrative Arcs
Arcs are traversal lenses (not a fixed order).
II. Six universal Conditions
Each Arc contains the same six Conditions (fractal thresholds at any scale).

Node labeling schema
Canonical IDs (recommended)
<ArcLetter><ConditionNumber> → D1..D6, R1..R6, E1..E6
Examples: D1, R3, E6
Abbreviation aliases (optional)
<ArcLetter><ConditionLetter> where:
Dawn D, Immersion I, Crucible C, Alignment A, Unveiling U, Return R
Examples:
DD = Descent / Dawn (= D1)
RC = Resonance / Crucible (= R3)
ER = Emergence / Return (= E6)

Universal node definition template
Each node is defined by:

Full node set
🌑 Descent Arc (D) — separation / fragmentation / descent into the Other
🌕 Resonance Arc (R) — relational echo / pattern recognition / mirror of the self
🌞 Emergence Arc (E) — symbolic integration / creative becoming / mythic synthesis

Motif mapping v3-min (2-motif)
Inventory (author once per project)
Define one concrete motif instance for each category:
O Object
A Action
Q Quality
B Being
F Force
M MetaSymbol
Each node uses exactly two motifs: Primary + Secondary.

Primary motif (locked per Condition)
Pattern across Conditions 1→6:
[ O, A, B, B, A, O ]
So:
C1 Dawn → O
C2 Immersion → A
C3 Crucible → B
C4 Alignment → B
C5 Unveiling → A
C6 Return → O
This creates the natural polarity pairing:
(1↔6) share O
(2↔5) share A
(3↔4) share B

Secondary motif (changes per Arc; ensures uniqueness)
Goal: every node has a unique (Primary, Secondary) pair, while nodes that share a condition remain related via shared Primary.
Because Primary uses {O,A,B} and Secondary can use {O,A,B,Q,F,M}, there are 3×6 = 18 possible ordered pairs, exactly matching 18 nodes.
Secondary sets per Condition (D/R/E)
Each condition gets a 3-slot secondary list (one per arc). For each primary group (two conditions), the two conditions use disjoint secondary sets, so no pair repeats.
C1 (Primary O): [Q, F, M]
C6 (Primary O): [O, A, B]
C2 (Primary A): [B, Q, F]
C5 (Primary A): [A, O, M]
C3 (Primary B): [O, Q, M]
C4 (Primary B): [A, B, F]
Arc order is fixed:
Descent = first
Resonance = second
Emergence = third

Full node mapping (Primary, Secondary)
Properties:
All 18 nodes unique by (Primary, Secondary).
Condition-relatedness preserved (shared Primary).
Polarity preserved via paired conditions sharing the same Primary, with complementary secondary sets.

Composition usage (minimal)
Primary = narrator lens / foreground anchor (what the node “is about” structurally).
Secondary = scene refraction / mid–background driver (what the node “means through”).
The implied third layer is the relationship between the two motifs (tension, harmony, inversion), not another motif.

Drop-in JSON
{
  "motif_mapping": {
    "version": "v3-min-2motif",
    "categories": ["O","A","Q","B","F","M"],
    "primary_by_condition": { "1":"O","2":"A","3":"B","4":"B","5":"A","6":"O" },
    "secondary_by_condition_arc": {
      "1": {"D":"Q","R":"F","E":"M"},
      "2": {"D":"B","R":"Q","E":"F"},
      "3": {"D":"O","R":"Q","E":"M"},
      "4": {"D":"A","R":"B","E":"F"},
      "5": {"D":"A","R":"O","E":"M"},
      "6": {"D":"O","R":"A","E":"B"}
    },
    "node_pairs": {
      "D1": {"primary":"O","secondary":"Q"},
      "R1": {"primary":"O","secondary":"F"},
      "E1": {"primary":"O","secondary":"M"},
      "D2": {"primary":"A","secondary":"B"},
      "R2": {"primary":"A","secondary":"Q"},
      "E2": {"primary":"A","secondary":"F"},
      "D3": {"primary":"B","secondary":"O"},
      "R3": {"primary":"B","secondary":"Q"},
      "E3": {"primary":"B","secondary":"M"},
      "D4": {"primary":"B","secondary":"A"},
      "R4": {"primary":"B","secondary":"B"},
      "E4": {"primary":"B","secondary":"F"},
      "D5": {"primary":"A","secondary":"A"},
      "R5": {"primary":"A","secondary":"O"},
      "E5": {"primary":"A","secondary":"M"},
      "D6": {"primary":"O","secondary":"O"},
      "R6": {"primary":"O","secondary":"A"},
      "E6": {"primary":"O","secondary":"B"}
    }
  }
}

If you want the original polarity pairs (1↔4, 2↔5, 3↔6) instead, the same two-motif scheme works; only primary_by_condition and the condition pairing groups change.


Compatibility note (optional)
If you retain v2 IDs for backwards references, treat v3 as a rename layer: Shadow/Mirror/Mythogenesis ⇢ Descent/Resonance/Emergence and Initiation/Encounter/Crisis/Harmony/Wisdom/Integration ⇢ Dawn/Immersion/Crucible/Alignment/Unveiling/Return; motif mapping rules remain identical.

Node Blueprint v3 audit (aligned to 2-motif system)
Keep (strong)
Sections I, II (minus old motif fields), III–V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, X.
Foreground/Midground/Background fields: still useful, but should be reframed so you don’t feel obligated to build 3 separate motif layers.
Fix (required)
Your current Motifs block is still the old “indexed + 6-motif” design (Primary/Secondary + Variable(4) and “Index _”). That conflicts with the simplified mapping you just chose.
Replace it with:
Primary motif category (locked by condition)
Secondary motif category (varies by arc)
Pair polarity note (how the two motifs oppose/align on your chosen spectrum)
Remove indexes entirely.
Tighten (optional but recommended)
“Node Key” duplicates Arc+Condition; keep it but make it derived (Arc.Condition).
Add a single “Narrator lens” line to formalize your foreground = narrator idea.

Minimal JSON template update (so tools don’t expect indices/variables)
If you’re feeding Universe-Forge, the motif section should be:

    "primary_category": "O",
    "secondary_category": "Q",
    "polarity_note": ""
  }
}

Key change: remove index and remove variable_motifs.
If you want, I can also regenerate the node_blueprint_v3.schema.json to enforce exactly these fields.
